public_rationale: A 2024 recall documents a concrete unusual-scenario hazard, while an independent driving evaluation finds substantial generalization failures across several planning methods. Together they support persistent edge-case difficulties and the absence of a demonstrated broad solution under the stated reading. Waymo's safety results and its completed recall remedy show that these difficulties coexist with effective deployment and specific fixes.
limitations: The absence of a validated broad solution is an inference from the examined evidence, not proof about every undisclosed system.
Aggregate safety improvements do not directly settle unfamiliar-scenario performance.
The result does not establish that edge cases will remain unsolved forever.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Edge cases remain a serious problem for driverless cars, with no generalizable solution yet.

statement.excerpt: In 2016 I warned that driverless cars would endlessly face edge cases; it’s still a serious problem. As yet there is no generalizable solution.

from_speaker: As yet there is no generalizable solution
our_interpretation: The claim describes the state of driverless driving at the post. Endlessly is part of the retrospective warning, not a separately scored infinite forecast.
A serious problem means unfamiliar scenarios can still cause material safety or operational failures.
No generalizable solution means no validated, broadly transferable solution had removed the difficulty across unfamiliar driving situations. It does not require literal zero risk.
The current state is assessed using the latest partial calendar year, January 1 through December 11, 2024, because incidents and technical evaluations are reported continuously.
The assessment concerns the supplied technical proposition, not whether Marcus first issued the warning in 2016.
criteria.support_condition: Contemporaneous safety records and technical evaluations show material failures in unusual driving situations and continuing limits to generalization across such situations.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A validated approach demonstrates robust transfer across materially varied unfamiliar driving situations, with evidence that edge cases no longer pose a serious operational or safety problem.

evidence.locator: Page 2, Description of the Safety Risk
evidence.explanation: Waymo's filing documents a utility-pole collision under a particular combination of mapping and perception conditions. It also records a software and map remedy, showing that this specific defect was addressed.

evidence.locator: Section IV-A, Generalization of state-of-the-art Planning Methods
evidence.explanation: The interPlan study tests difficult scenarios and finds failures among both learned and rule-based planners. Its improved hybrid planner is evidence of progress, but the study does not demonstrate a broadly solved generalization problem.

evidence.locator: Section How the Waymo Driver Reduces Crash Rates
evidence.explanation: Waymo reports fewer injury and airbag-deployment crashes than its human benchmarks over more than 22 million driverless miles. These aggregate results show substantial practical success, but do not directly measure generalization to unfamiliar edge cases.
